newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Strauss to take early control of Israel's Elite.
newsitem.headline: Strauss to take early control of Israel's Elite.

text.p: The head of Israel's Strauss family and Elite Industries chief executive David Federman have agreed to move up the date for the transfer to Strauss of control in Elite, Israel's leading coffee and chocolate maker, a newspaper said on Thursday.
Spokesmen for Strauss and Elite said they were checking the report.
The Strauss family, through its Gideon Holdings company, announced earlier this month it was buying the Federman family's stake in Elite and the transfer would take place in mid-July.

But the Globes financial daily said Michael Strauss, head of the Strauss family and chairman and chief executive of privately held Strauss Dairies, reached an agreement with the Federman group to make the transfer in early June.
The move is aimed at reducing uncertainty in the company and implementing a reorganisation as soon as possible.
The first stage includes creating a structure under which Elite will become a holding company and its various divisions subsidiaries, Globes said.
Strauss is paying 226.86 million shekels ($66 million) for the Federman group's 13 percent equity holding and 26.8 percent voting rights of Elite.
The deal will give Strauss 30.69 percent of the equity and 46.24 percent of voting rights in Elite.
The purchase resolved an agreement between the partners, who have been feuding over running Elite, whereby one would buy out the other's shares.
Elite has undergone far-reaching changes since the Strauss family came on the scene. Much of its loss-making European businesses, acquired in 1992, have been closed or sold off.
